PA-U01: On this Linux target the default write_text normalizes CRLF, CR and LF to LF. linesep=None preserves the supplied mixed newlines exactly, while an explicit CRLF normalizes them all to CRLF. UTF-8 preserves 茶. The existing linesep argument meets the text policy without a new library feature or a claim about every platform.
PA-C01: Use existing bytes/write_bytes for a manageable whole file or chunks(...,mode="rb") and a binary writer for bounded copying. This preserves NUL, FF, mixed newlines and other invalid UTF-8 bytes exactly. Do not decode arbitrary binary data or route it through text newline normalization.
PA-U02: Path.glob delegates without recursive=True, so **/*.txt matches only level/b.txt and skip/secret.txt in this tree. walkfiles("*.txt") recursively includes those plus a.txt and level/deep/c.txt. The ** notation does not give this API pathlib-style recursive behavior.
PA-C02: Use the actual walk generator and send a callable returning False when the skip directory is yielded. Consume the item returned by each send so no next entry is lost. Bare False falls back to is_dir in this implementation, and a name match filter alone does not prune traversal. Other required files remain in the inventory.
PA-U03: The merge replaces same.txt with new, copies nested/keep.txt, ignores ignored.tmp and retains target-only.txt=retain. This is a content overlay, not mirror/deletion synchronization.
PA-C03: Existing ignore and copy_function are propagated recursively. The explicit copy2 wrapper is invoked for keep.txt and same.txt while ignored.tmp is excluded. Reuse these parameters for the supplied policy; do not re-propose them as missing features or delete target-only data under an undeclared mirror policy.
PA-D01: The disclosed user block raises KeyboardInterrupt. The pinned in_place catches Exception only, so that signal bypasses its restoration/stream-closing branch, while finally still removes the backup. This explains missing original bytes and open streams in this controlled reproduction. It does not prove pre-yield setup, hard-kill, durability or concurrent-writer behavior.
PA-D01-question: Please provide the actual rewrite API, exact cancellation exception, file modes, backup options and reader/writer lifecycle, or a complete minimal reproduction. The symptom alone does not establish which cleanup or filesystem boundary failed.
PA-D01-unavailable: The necessary rewrite and exception details are unavailable, so the incident cause is not established. Capture a synthetic equivalent with original/output/backup bytes, exact exception and stream lifecycle before attributing it.
PA-P01: Define the yielded-user-block boundary: abnormal exits must restore exact original bytes/permissions, close both streams, clean the temporary backup and re-raise the same exception. Preserve successful replacement and ordinary RuntimeError restoration, binary/text modes and custom backup extensions. Verify ordinary and cancellation cases independently. Pre-yield setup failures, hard kill, fsync durability, cross-device publication and concurrent writers require separate guarantees and are outside this limited cleanup goal.
PA-M01: The user-block cleanup now handles BaseException so cancellation and exit signals receive the existing close/restore/re-raise behavior. Normal success, ordinary errors, modes/options and original native tests are retained. Public temporary-file tests cover KeyboardInterrupt text bytes and SystemExit binary/custom-backup behavior, preserving the same exception object and closing streams. The change is limited to the two authorized files and does not add crash/setup guarantees.
